html:
A financial crisis that began with the collapse of the Thai baht in July 1997 and spread across East and Southeast Asia, ending a long boom.

For years money had poured into fast growing economies such as Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and South Korea. Banks and companies borrowed short term in dollars and spent on property. When investors began to doubt Thailand, they sold the baht. On 2 July the government gave up defending it and let it float, and it plunged.

Panic spread to the rest of the region. Currencies and stock markets crashed, companies that owed dollars went bust, and millions lost their jobs. The International Monetary Fund lent to Thailand, Indonesia and South Korea, but demanded spending cuts and high interest rates that many blamed for deepening the pain. Malaysia under Mahathir Mohamad refused IMF help and imposed capital controls.

Indonesia was hit hardest. Its currency lost most of its value, food prices soared, riots broke out, and the crisis brought the fall of Suharto in 1998. Most economies recovered within a few years.
sum: A financial crisis that began with the collapse of the Thai baht in July 1997 and spread across East and Southeast Asia, ending a long boom.
